column2: Buran-19, this is... no one. Baikonur is silent. Two beacons are still calling, close by. Sasha. Lena. Bring them home.
The hull is holding. But we need metal to get home. The laser is charged. Burn the rocks, then pull the pieces in.
Static on every channel. The radar is going blind. Three more of ours are out there. If the discharge comes for you, let it close. Then hit the pulse.
There it is. The rift. Three of ours are circling its edge, too close. Stay outside the ring: what goes in comes out broken. If something hunts you, the shelters will hide you.
The station's cargo is still drifting out here. Some crates are sealed, some are burnt. Scan before you open them. Six crates, and we can keep going.
Four voices on the beacon now. And the whole field is awake. You know everything you need. Use it. Bring them home.
Baikonur. November, nineteen eighty-eight.
Buran flew once. No one was aboard.
Two orbits. A perfect landing.
Then the program was closed.
Nineteen ninety-one.
One man stayed in orbit... while the country below him disappeared.
But the program went on. In secret.
A light in orbit no one could explain. They named it Object nineteen... and sent Buran to it.
The experiment failed.
The crew was scattered across the field.
And at the centre... the rift opened.
Baikonur, this is Buran-19.
Baikonur...
Do you copy?
No one answers.
Bring them home.
But where... is home?
No more beacons. Just the field, and you. Hold on as long as you can.
The field is waking up. Keep moving.
More of them now. The shelters will hide you... for a while.
The hull is singing. Something out there is getting stronger.
The rift is growing. Everything is falling toward it.
This is the collapse. Nothing holds now. Make it count.
Twelve aboard. The cabin is full of breathing again.
But the rift is still open. And it is growing.
Something is clinging to the hull. The counters are dropping. Radiation feeds on us while it holds on. The rockets will tear it off. Three more voices out here.
The fuel is falling, and we are not burning it. Magnets. They latch on and drink. Keep the tanks full: canisters are drifting nearby.
They are coming in packs now. Too many to outrun. The freeze charge stops all of them at once, for a while. Use it when they close in.
Deep field. Rock and wreckage everywhere. Burn the metal and pull it in: it charges the ram. Then let the ram do the work.
A storm of discharges. They will blind the radar and kill the laser. Pulse them away, then hide in a shelter to get your shield back. Four of ours are in the storm.
The voice again. Come to the rift, it says. Five beacons around it. The field is collapsing, faster every minute. Do not wait.
Then, through the static...
a voice.
Not Baikonur.
Buran-19... we see you.
Come to the rift.
The voice knows our names.
It is the commander of Object nineteen. He went into the rift in nineteen ninety-one.
Inside, he says, it is still nineteen ninety-one.
And the way home is open.
We went in. All of us.
No sound. No time. Only the light.
Then... Earth. Blue, and whole.
Buran-19, this is Baikonur.
We hear you.
Welcome home.
His crew is still out here. Their beacons are old, the signals weak. Radiation and magnets everywhere. Four to bring home.
The station's graveyard. Everything that broke is drifting toward the rift. We need metal for the hull before we go in. Fifty pieces.
The field is guarding the way. Discharges and packs, all around the cargo we need. Six crates. Take them and run.
The tide is turning. The rift pulls harder every minute. Five more of ours on its edge. Be quick.
The radar is dead. Nothing on the screen now. Only your eyes, and the beacons. Find four of them.
This is the threshold. Everything the field has, it throws at us now. Six voices. The last ones.
He is waiting at the edge of the rift. The last one. Bring him aboard, then follow the light home.
This is Radio Mayak. Moscow time, twenty-one hours.
Prices will rise again from Monday. Queues outside the bakeries since dawn.
The Baltic republics have declared...
Moscow. August nineteenth. Tanks are on the streets.
The committee has declared a state of emergency. Swan Lake on every channel.
Crowds outside the White House. They are building barricades.
The coup has failed. The committee members have been arrested.
Leningrad will be called Saint Petersburg again.
Ukraine votes for independence.
No one knows who pays the cosmonauts now.
The cosmonaut aboard Mir is still in orbit. His return has been postponed again.
The treaty is signed. The union... no longer exists.
December twenty-fifth. The red flag over the Kremlin has been lowered.
A new flag. A new anthem, soon. A new country.
Baikonur now stands in another state.
The space program has no budget for next year.
Moscow time... midnight.
Is anyone still listening on this frequency?
Baikonur calling Buran-19. Baikonur calling Buran-19.
Every one of them came home.
Not all of us came home. We say their names.
And somewhere out there, one of ours is still waiting.
